usdRate.sourceName: European Central Bank euro reference rate (USD)
usdRate.note: EUR 1 = USD 1.1172, so about EUR 0.895 per US dollar; World Bank 2025 average 0.885.

inflation_cpi.sourceName: Trading Economics (National Statistics Office Malta, September 2026)
inflation_cpi.note: Annual inflation 2.4% in September 2026 (2.0% in August), released 16 October 2026; secondary source because nso.gov.mt refused automated access. World Bank 2025 average 2.4%.

inflation_projection.sourceName: ECB 2% medium-term target; Malta inflation 2.4% (Sep 2026) and 2.4% (2025)
inflation_projection.note: Malta's inflation has run slightly above the euro-area target in recent years, so 2.5% is used for planning.

policy_rate.sourceName: European Central Bank, deposit facility rate
policy_rate.note: Malta uses the euro; ECB deposit facility rate 2.50% (main refinancing rate 2.65%) from 16 September 2026.

savings_account_rate.sourceName: ECB MFI interest rate statistics: Maltese banks, household overnight deposits (new business)
savings_account_rate.note: Average 0.07% on household overnight deposits in August 2026; deposits redeemable at up to 3 months' notice paid 1.74%.

fdr_3m_rate.note: ECB/Central Bank of Malta MFI statistics publish household deposits with agreed maturity up to 1 year as one bucket (2.24% in August 2026); no 3-month rate was found.

fdr_1y_rate.sourceName: ECB MFI interest rate statistics: Maltese banks, household deposits with agreed maturity up to 1 year (new business)
fdr_1y_rate.note: Bucket covers all fixed terms up to one year (1.99% in June, 2.12% in July 2026).

dps_rate.note: No monthly recurring deposit product with a published average rate was found for Malta.

bank_deposit_avg_rate.sourceName: ECB MFI interest rate statistics: Maltese banks, household deposits with agreed maturity (outstanding amounts)
bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: Average rate on all outstanding household term deposits; World Bank FR.INR.DPST has no Malta figure.

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: The Treasury sells retail government savings bonds (including the 62+ Savings Bond for older people), but treasury.gov.mt refused automated access and no current rate was read.

tbill_91d_rate.note: Malta auctions 3-month treasury bills, but the Treasury and Central Bank of Malta pages refused automated access and no recent auction yield was found.

tbond_5y_rate.note: No current 5-year Malta Government Stock yield was found; the Central Bank of Malta site refused automated access and only the ECB 10-year convergence yield was available.

tbond_10y_rate.sourceName: ECB long-term interest rate for convergence purposes (10-year government bond), Malta
tbond_10y_rate.note: Monthly average for September 2026 (3.90% in August).

tax_bank_interest.note: Not confirmed: PwC's Malta corporate withholding table (reviewed 30 Sep 2026) shows 25% on interest to resident individuals, while its individual pages mention an optional final withholding tax on investment income without a rate; the Tax and Customs Administration pages refused automated access.

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: The tax rate on interest from Malta government savings bonds could not be confirmed on an official page (Treasury and tax administration pages refused automated access).

deposit_insurance_limit.note: EUR 100,000 per depositor per bank; up to EUR 500,000 extra for temporary high balances from certain life events credited within six months before a default.

credit_card_rate_cap.note: No legal cap or published average credit card rate for Malta was found; the Central Bank of Malta site refused automated access.

equity_return_low.sourceName: MSE Share Index about 4,278 on 30 Oct 2026; its September 2026 peak of 4,404 was only the highest since July 2024
equity_return_low.note: Low case: the small Maltese market keeps its weak decade-long record.

equity_return_base.sourceName: MSE Share Index (Trading Economics); 1-year deposit 2.24% less an assumed 15% tax = 1.9%
equity_return_base.note: Base case kept within about 3 points of the after-tax safe rate because the local index has a weak 10-year record; most savers would use a diversified euro equity fund.

equity_return_high.sourceName: Global equity long-run returns in euros; MSE Share Index (Trading Economics)
equity_return_high.note: High case: a diversified euro equity fund matching long-run global equity returns of about 7-8% in euros.

gold_return_low.note: Low case: gold barely keeps up after the 2025-26 spike, with no help from the euro.

gold_return_base.sourceName: Gold price history (Trading Economics); ECB 2% inflation target
gold_return_base.note: Base case: dollar gold rises roughly with world inflation plus a little, and the euro is assumed stable against the dollar over the long run.

gold_return_high.note: High case: a repeat of gold's strong 2005-2025 trend in euro terms.

fixed_income_return_low.sourceName: Household deposits up to 1 year 2.24% (Aug 2026) less an assumed 15% final tax, with ECB rates able to fall
fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case: term deposits after tax if rates fall back.

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: Deposits up to 1 year 2.24% and 10-year government bond 4.19%, both less an assumed 15% tax
fixed_income_return_base.note: Base case: mostly term deposits at about 1.9% after tax, with some Malta Government Stocks.

fixed_income_return_high.sourceName: Malta 10-year government bond 4.19% (Sep 2026) less an assumed 15% tax = 3.6%
fixed_income_return_high.note: High case: holding long Malta Government Stocks.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: The Malta Financial Services Authority does not publish an industry life claim settlement ratio that could be found.

insurance_term_premium_table.note: Term life is sold, but no published premium table or regulator data on term premiums per sum insured was found.

health_hospitalisation_cost.note: Planned and emergency care in public hospitals is free for insured residents (European Commission guide, July 2026); no official figure for a typical out-of-pocket private hospital stay was found.

health_premium_table.note: No private health insurance premium table per EUR 100,000 of cover was found from the regulator or another public source.

goal_inflation_health.sourceName: Trading Economics (NSO Malta): health inflation 2.9% in September 2026
goal_inflation_health.note: Health prices rise a little faster than headline inflation and medical costs usually outrun it over decades, so 3.5% is used.

goal_inflation_education.sourceName: Trading Economics (NSO Malta): education inflation 3.2% in September 2026; ECB HICP Malta education 4.3% in December 2025
goal_inflation_education.note: Education prices (largely private and church schools and tuition) rise faster than headline inflation; 4% is used for planning.

life_expectancy.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects via georank.org
life_expectancy.note: Men 81.9, women 85.6 (UN WPP estimate for 2026); World Bank 2024 figure 83.0.

life_table_remaining.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects via georank.org
life_table_remaining.note: Remaining years computed from georank's expected age at death by current age (UN WPP 2026 estimate).

support_ratio.sourceName: World Bank SP.POP.DPND.OL (2025); UN WPP 2024 via populationpyramid.net (2040, 2065)
support_ratio.note: 100 / old-age dependency ratio: 30.9 (2025, World Bank), 38.3 (2040) and 80.9 (2065, populationpyramid.net/malta/2065/).

retirement_age_default.sourceName: European Commission, Your social security rights in Malta (July 2026)
retirement_age_default.note: Pensionable age is 65 for everyone born on or after 1 January 1962, men and women; early pension from 61 needs 42 years of contributions (35 paid) for those born from 1976.

retirement_age_government.sourceName: European Commission, Your social security rights in Malta (July 2026)
retirement_age_government.note: Public employees are insured under the same Social Security Act two-thirds pension, so the same pensionable age of 65 applies; the guide does not give a separate civil-service age, and older Treasury service pensions apply only to long-serving staff.

retirement_return_low.sourceName: Household deposits up to 1 year 2.24% less an assumed 15% tax, with rates able to fall
retirement_return_low.note: Low case: bank deposits after tax if ECB rates fall.

retirement_return_base.sourceName: Household deposits up to 1 year 2.24% (Aug 2026) less an assumed 15% tax = 1.9%
retirement_return_base.note: Base case capped at the after-tax 1-year term deposit rate, as no treasury bill yield was found.

retirement_return_high.sourceName: Malta 10-year government bond 4.19% less an assumed 15% tax = 3.6%
retirement_return_high.note: High case: a ladder of Malta Government Stocks and retail savings bonds, below the current after-tax 10-year yield.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.sourceName: After-tax 1-year deposit 1.9%; MSE index weak record
retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case for a balanced mix if shares lag.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.sourceName: After-tax deposits 1.9%, government bonds 3.6%; equity base 5%
retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Base case: roughly half shares at 5% and half deposits and bonds at about 2-3.5% after tax.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.note: High case for a growth-leaning balanced mix.

old_age_allowance_monthly.sourceName: European Commission, Your social security rights in Malta (July 2026)
old_age_allowance_monthly.note: Age Pension (means-tested, for residents 60+ without a contributory pension): highest rate EUR 166.79 a week for a single person (EUR 199.56 for a couple), converted at 52/12 weeks a month.

old_age_allowance_eligibility.sourceName: European Commission, Your social security rights in Malta (July 2026)
old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: Paid from 60 to people who do not qualify for a contributory pension and pass income and capital tests (capital below EUR 16,000 single, EUR 26,000 couple).

gratuity_rule.note: No statutory end-of-service gratuity for private employees was found in the European Commission guide or other sources read; Maltese employment law pages (gov.mt) could not be checked.

public_pension_scheme.sourceName: European Commission, Your social security rights in Malta (July 2026)
public_pension_scheme.note: Contributory two-thirds Retirement Pension under the Social Security Act (employee and employer 10% each in 2026 per PwC), based on the best 10 of the last 41-42 years; the guide says pensions get yearly cost-of-living increases (survivors') and invalidity rates follow cost of living and income.

dps.note: No standard monthly recurring deposit scheme with published rates was found.

sanchayapatra_5y.localNameEn: Malta Government savings bonds (62+ Savings Bond for people aged 62 and over)
sanchayapatra_5y.note: Sold to individuals by the Treasury; current rate and general eligibility not confirmed.

tbill_91d.note: Auctioned by the Treasury; individuals can bid.

equity_fund.note: EU UCITS funds and ETFs are sold to retail investors.

gold.note: No restriction on buying physical gold.

centralBank.name: Bank Ċentrali ta' Malta (Central Bank of Malta)
centralBank.note: Part of the Eurosystem; monetary policy set by the European Central Bank.

insuranceComplaints.name: Office of the Arbiter for Financial Services

pensionScheme.name: Department of Social Security (Contributory Retirement Pension)

publicHealthCover.name: Ministry for Health and Active Ageing (free public health care)
